text: For the choirmaster. On a stringed instrument. Of David.

versions.text: For the choirmaster. With stringed instruments. Of David.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew נְגִינַת is singular here (unlike the plural נְגִינוֹת found in other superscriptions). Rendering it as singular is more precise, though the difference is slight.

text: Hear my cry, O God; listen to my prayer.
From the end of the earth I call to you when my heart grows faint; lead me to the rock that is higher than I.
For you have been my refuge, a strong tower against the enemy.
Let me dwell in your tent forever, and take refuge in the shelter of your wings. Selah
For you, O God, have heard my vows; you have given me the heritage of those who fear your name.
May you add days to the days of the king; may his years reach through generation after generation.

versions.text: Add days to the days of the king; may his years span many generations.
versions.explanation: The verb תּוֹסִיף is second-person addressed to God, and the second line echoes the idiom דֹר וָדֹר. Matching the two lines as parallel petitions gives smoother rhythm for reading aloud and reflects the repeated-generation idiom.

text: May he be enthroned forever before God; appoint your steadfast love and faithfulness to guard him.
Then I will sing praise to your name forever, fulfilling my vows day after day.
